dialog.switchBody: This clears the canvas so you can start fresh at the new level.

file.saveBody: Your chain is saved as a file (usually in your Downloads folder). Open it again later with File → Open.
file.pictureTitle: Save a picture of your chain
file.pictureBody: A PNG picture of everything on the canvas — for a worksheet or a chat. The chain is hidden inside the picture too: File → Open turns it back into the chain.
file.downloadBody: The whole app in one file. Double-click it and it opens in your web browser — no internet, nothing to install. Copy it to a USB stick or a shared folder for a class; saved chains open in it too. For a newer version later, download it again. (This website also works offline once you have visited it: your browser keeps a copy.)
file.openBody: There are already elements on the canvas. Replace them with this chain, or add it beside them?
file.levelReplace: It was made at the {level} level: replacing the canvas switches the app to {level}.
file.levelAdd: It was made at the {level} level, so the app switches to {level}.

file.linkCopied: Link copied. Anyone who opens it gets a copy of this chain.
file.linkLong: Link copied — but it is very long, so some chat apps may cut it short. Saving a file is safer.

file.linkBroken: This link is broken or cut short, so the chain could not be opened. Ask for the link again.
file.pictureSaved: Picture saved — usually in your Downloads folder.
file.pictureFailed: The picture could not be made. Try again, or save a file instead.
file.notChain: This file isn't a saved signal chain. Open a .json file or a picture saved from this app.
file.noChainInPicture: This picture has no chain inside. Only pictures saved from this app can be opened.

tools.label: What a click does
tools.dragHint: Drag an element to move it. Drag empty space to look around the canvas.
tools.selectHint: Click elements to pick several (click again to drop one), or drag a box around them. Then right-click one to copy or duplicate them all.
tools.removeHint: Click an element or a wire to remove it.
tools.redoHint: Bring back the change you just took back.

connecting.hint: Click a highlighted input. Click empty space to add a bend.

warnings.domainMixedBus: Silent — analog and digital signals can't be mixed. Pass the digital ones through a Digital to Analog Converter first.
warnings.digitalSignal: Silent — the signal is digital. Pass it through a Digital to Analog Converter first.
warnings.adcExpectsAnalog: Silent — the signal is already digital.
warnings.dacExpectsDigital: Silent — the signal is analog. Put an Analog to Digital Converter before this one.
warnings.encoderNeedsDigital: Silent — an Encoder works only on a digital signal. Put an Analog to Digital Converter before it.
warnings.dawNeedsDigital: Silent — a computer records only numbers. Put an Analog to Digital Converter before it.

eq.label: Parametric Equalizer
eq.graphHint: Drag a coloured dot up to make that range louder, down to make it quieter, or sideways to move it to lower or higher sounds. Double-click a dot to set it back to 0 dB (no change).
eq.graphHintWidth: Scroll over a dot to make its band wider or narrower.

graphic-eq.label: Graphic EQ
graphic-eq.hint: Drag a slider up to boost that frequency, down to cut it. Double-click = 0 dB.

speaker.needsAmp: No sound — a passive speaker needs an amplifier before it
speaker.distorted: Bad sound — something before it distorts

active-speaker.label: Active Speaker
active-speaker.blown: Blown! An amplifier's output is far too strong for it.

headphones.label: Headphones
headphones.needsGain: No sound — headphones need a Gain knob right before them
headphones.blown: Blown! An amplifier's output is far too strong for them.

di-box.micLevel: mic level · to the desk's Preamp
di-box.instrumentLevel: instrument level · to a guitar amp

instrument.needsDi: No DI Box: the high notes get lost

start.intro: Learn Signal Chain shows what happens to a sound on its way to the speakers, a recording or a stream. You build the chain yourself, element by element, and each element shows what reaches it. The app does not explain what each element is — that is the teacher's part. It shows what the chain does.
points: Choose a level at the top: **Beginner**, **Intermediate** or **Advanced**.
Open the elements panel (the button at the top left) and drag an element onto the canvas. On an empty canvas, the highlighted tile is a good first pick.
Click an element's output (a ring on its right side), then the input of another element (a ring on its left side). A wire joins them.
Follow the sound: at Beginner, each speaker, recorder or stream says whether sound reaches it; from Intermediate, the meters show how strong it is.

build.intro: Everything works with the mouse, and there are no modes to switch: point at a port and you are wiring; point anywhere else and you are moving things.
points: **Add** — drag an element from the elements panel onto the canvas. Drop it onto a wire and it goes into that wire, between the two elements the wire joins (when it can go there).
**Wire** — click an output, then one of the inputs that light up. Click empty space on the way to add a bend. Esc or a right-click stops.
One output can feed several inputs: click it again to start another wire.
**Unplug** — point at a connected input: it turns into a red ×. Click it. An input holding several wires lists them, so you can pick one.

**Right-click an element** to bypass it (the signal passes through unchanged), flip it, cut, copy, duplicate or remove it. Right-click empty canvas to paste, select everything or insert a saved chain.

**What a click does** (bottom left): **Drag** moves elements, and the canvas when you drag empty space. **Select** picks several elements. **Remove** removes what you click. **Undo** and **Redo** are there too.
Turn a knob or move a fader by dragging it with the left mouse button.

**Snap to grid** (at the top) lines elements up as you move them. Zoom with the mouse wheel or the buttons at the bottom left; zoomed far out, the elements show less detail, so a big chain stays readable.
Keys: {mod}Z undo, {mod}Y redo, {mod}C copy, {mod}X cut, {mod}V paste, {mod}D duplicate, {mod}A select everything, Delete removes what is selected.

levels.intro: Each level shows the sound system at its own scale. Switching level clears the canvas (the app asks first), and every level starts empty.
points: **Beginner — the room.** The devices and how they connect: voices and instruments, microphones, a stage box, a mixing desk, a computer, speakers, a recorder, a stream. No numbers: each speaker, recorder or stream simply says whether sound reaches it.
**Intermediate — a small mixing desk.** You build the desk's channel yourself, one control at a time. The meters show how strong the signal is, its peaks and its noise, and they move with the sound.

**Advanced — the parts and the digital side.** The full processors, the converters that turn sound into numbers and back, and a stream. After a converter, levels are digital, in dBFS: 0 dBFS is the very top, and nothing can go above it.

meters.intro: From Intermediate, the app plays a short loop of real sound through the chain — a voice, drums, music — silently, inside your browser, and measures it at every element. The meters show what it measured. You hear nothing: the app makes no sound.
points: The solid bar is the average level. The pale part above it is the peaks — the loudest moments. A thin line holds the highest peak for a few seconds. The blue part at the bottom is the noise: what is left when the music stops.
The colours belong to the scale: blue up to the noise, green up to 0 dB, yellow above it, red at the very top.
The word under a meter is the verdict on the whole loop:
Clipping is judged on the peaks: a drum hit can clip while its average still looks fine.
**Peak**, **RMS** (the average) and **Noise** under a meter give the numbers.
Where the sound is in the air — a voice, a drum kit, a speaker — the meter shows how loud it is to the ear, in dB SPL.
The ring around each port shows the health of the signal there. Grey means nothing is connected.
A short note on an element says when something is wrong, such as **Not connected**.
At Beginner there are no meters to read: each speaker, recorder or stream says whether sound reaches it.

health.too-quiet: so weak it is close to the noise
health.hot: strong, with less room left before it distorts
health.clipping: the peaks hit the top: the sound is distorted

wires.intro: One wire carries the whole signal — a stereo signal too.
points: A stereo wire is drawn as a double line. An output that carries only the left or the right side shows an **L** or an **R**.
From Intermediate, a wire's colour shows where its sound ends up:
**Red** means the sound on that wire clips, or something is wrong there. A **grey** wire carries nothing.
A dotted wire is sound in the air: from a voice, a drum kit or an amp to a microphone.
Wires that carry sound move in the direction the sound flows.
At Beginner, every wire has the same colour.

colours.main: To the Master Bus — the main mix
colours.record: Into an Audio Interface, or to a stream

save.intro: The canvas is kept in this browser: close the app, and your chain is there when you come back.
points: **File → Save to a file** saves the chain as a file, to open later or send to someone.
**File → Save as a picture** saves a picture for a worksheet or a chat. The chain is hidden inside it: **File → Open** turns the picture back into the chain.
**File → Copy a share link** copies a link. Anyone who opens it gets their own copy of the chain.
**File → Open** opens a saved file or picture. **File → New** clears the canvas.
**File → Download the app** saves the whole app as one file. Double-click it and it opens in the web browser, with no internet. Copy it to a USB stick or a shared folder for a class.
For a lesson: build a chain beforehand and share its link or file. Each student gets their own copy to change.

examples.intro: Open a chain to see it work, then change it. On an empty canvas it simply opens; otherwise the app asks whether it replaces what is there or goes beside it. The app switches to the chain's level.

singer.name: A singer on two speakers
singer.about: A voice, a microphone, the mixing desk and two active speakers.

band.name: A band on stage
band.about: Voice, drums, guitar and keyboard through a stage box into the mixing desk. The main mix goes to an amplifier and two passive speakers, the monitor mix to a stage monitor.

recording.name: Recording a voice
recording.about: A microphone into an audio interface, recorded on a computer. The computer's sound comes back out to two studio monitors.

vocalChannel.name: A vocal channel
vocalChannel.about: Microphone, preamp, high-pass filter, equalizer and compressor, then the fader and pan into the master bus and two speakers.

monitorMix.name: A monitor mix
monitorMix.about: A voice into the main mix, and also, at its own level, into an aux bus that feeds a stage monitor.

guitarDi.name: A guitar with a DI box
guitarDi.about: The DI box sends the guitar to the desk and to its amp. A microphone on the amp gives a second channel. Both meet in the master bus.

converters.name: Through the converters
converters.about: A voice turned into numbers, processed digitally, and turned back into a signal for a speaker.

stream.name: A live stream
stream.about: A voice channel, digital after the converter, into the master bus, packed by an encoder and sent out as a stream.
